# keyframes.js — the agent surface, full (llms-full.txt)

Generated from `docs/published-surface.md` (the machine-checked
published-export manifest) + the `proof:*` gate roster. Verified by
`proof:agent-surface`: the index can never advertise an export the
surface does not publish, nor cite a gate that does not exist.

README: https://github.com/mkbabb/keyframes.js/blob/master/README.md

## The round-trip recipe (kf's unique axis-1)

```ts
// THE ROUND-TRIP (kf's unique axis: author CSS is the source format).
// PARSE  author CSS @keyframes  → an animation object
// ANIMATE that object over any element / plain object / scroll
// SERIALIZE it BACK to valid CSS (the parser run backward — compileToCSS)
//
// The agent's INPUT format IS the library's SOURCE format: every other
// library makes the agent TRANSLATE CSS into a bespoke tween syntax; kf
// does not. This is why kf has an agent surface no competitor can write.

import { loadAnimationEngine } from "@mkbabb/keyframes.js";

// ONE await loads the CSS engine (and value.js with it); cached thereafter.
const { CSSKeyframesAnimation, compileToCSS } = await loadAnimationEngine();

// PARSE — feed it the SAME CSS @keyframes a stylesheet would carry:
const anim = new CSSKeyframesAnimation({ duration: 2000 }).fromString(`
    @keyframes slide {
        from { transform: translateX(-100%); background-color: #C462D8; }
        100% { transform: translateX(50%);   background-color: #E85252; }
    }
`);

// ANIMATE — colors interpolate in perceptual oklab by default [axis-2]:
anim.setTargets(document.getElementById("box"));
anim.play();

// SERIALIZE — back to a pure, zero-runtime CSS artifact (the backward half):
const { css, eligible, refusals } = compileToCSS(anim);
// `css` is a @keyframes block + animation shorthand; `refusals` names what
// cannot round-trip faithfully (never a silent approximation).
```

## The curated primitive index

- **CSSKeyframesAnimation** — parse author CSS @keyframes → animate any element/object; the round-trippable source-of-truth axis [axis-1]
  - exports: `CSSKeyframesAnimation`, `Animation`, `loadAnimationEngine` · proof: `proof:roundtrip-fidelity` · docs: https://github.com/mkbabb/keyframes.js/blob/master/README.md#csskeyframesanimation
- **animate** — the single-call front door: construct + target + play, dispatched on input shape (CSS string / vars / motion-path spec)
  - exports: `animate` · proof: `proof:engine-correctness` · docs: https://github.com/mkbabb/keyframes.js/blob/master/README.md#animate
- **AnimationGroup** — composite many animations with replace/add/weighted layer blending (spatial composition)
  - exports: `AnimationGroup`, `defaultLayerConfig` · proof: `proof:blend` · docs: https://github.com/mkbabb/keyframes.js/blob/master/README.md#animationgroup
- **Sequence** — master-playhead temporal orchestration beside AnimationGroup's spatial blend
  - exports: `Sequence` · proof: `proof:orchestration` · docs: https://github.com/mkbabb/keyframes.js/blob/master/README.md#sequence
- **compileToCSS** — the round-trip's BACKWARD half: an orchestration graph → a pure zero-runtime CSS artifact (the parser run backward; GSAP/Motion cannot do this) [axis-1]
  - exports: `compileToCSS` · proof: `proof:compile-replay` · docs: https://github.com/mkbabb/keyframes.js/blob/master/README.md#the-dynamic-engine--loadanimationengine
- **fromStyleSheets** — INGEST: read the live web's own CSS @keyframes back into kf animations (CSSOM → CSSKeyframesAnimation), CORS-skip diagnostics never a silent drop [axis-1]
  - exports: `fromStyleSheets`, `fromLiveAnimations`, `adoptRunning` · proof: `proof:ingest-replay` · docs: https://github.com/mkbabb/keyframes.js/blob/master/README.md#the-dynamic-engine--loadanimationengine
- **ScrollScene** — scroll-driven animation as CSS: parse animation-timeline/-range, drive on the compositor where eligible and shipped physics where not, serialize back to valid CSS [axis-1]
  - exports: `ScrollScene`, `createScrollScene`, `roundTripScrollCSS` · proof: `proof:scroll-roundtrip` · docs: https://github.com/mkbabb/keyframes.js/blob/master/README.md#timeline
- **SpringProgress** — closed-form spring physics tracker; reseatToSpring for velocity-continuous interruption; the linear() twin is round-trippable
  - exports: `SpringProgress`, `reseatToSpring`, `probeVelocity` · proof: `proof:spring-blend-weight` · docs: https://github.com/mkbabb/keyframes.js/blob/master/README.md#springprogress
- **springTimingFunction** — spring physics → a typed Easing ({ fn, css }) / a CSS linear() stops string — a spring you can hand to native CSS [axis-1]
  - exports: `springTimingFunction`, `springLinearStops` · proof: `proof:roundtrip-easing` · docs: https://github.com/mkbabb/keyframes.js/blob/master/README.md#springlinearstops--springtimingfunction
- **stagger** — pure construction-time per-index delay distribution (materializes into the compiled CSS)
  - exports: `stagger` · proof: `proof:orchestration` · docs: https://github.com/mkbabb/keyframes.js/blob/master/README.md#stagger
- **Timeline** — progress driver (sample → clamp → easing → boundary-snap → smoothing); ScrollTimeline/ManualTimeline/createNativeTimeline variants — the caller owns the loop
  - exports: `Timeline`, `ScrollTimeline`, `ManualTimeline`, `createNativeTimeline` · proof: `proof:sync-step` · docs: https://github.com/mkbabb/keyframes.js/blob/master/README.md#timeline
- **NumericAnimation** — zero-alloc keyframe interpolation over { key: number } objects — animate any plain object, no DOM
  - exports: `NumericAnimation` · proof: `proof:zero-alloc` · docs: https://github.com/mkbabb/keyframes.js/blob/master/README.md#numericanimation
- **loadAnimationEngine** — the one gateway to the HEAVY tier: an awaited dynamic import that carries the CSS parser + value.js; light-only consumers never pay it [axis-3]
  - exports: `loadAnimationEngine` · proof: `proof:boundary` · docs: https://github.com/mkbabb/keyframes.js/blob/master/README.md#the-dynamic-engine--loadanimationengine

## The proof corpus (the public capability ledger)

Every claim above is signed by a CI-executed gate. The proof corpus
is itself a public artifact: run `npm run proof:all` to execute the
full roster (~133 `proof:*` gates). Each gate is a self-describing capability
claim — not "the library claims X" but "the library PROVES X, here
is the gate, here is the runnable snippet CI executes".
